chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

key_terms.الِازْدِيَادَ: Progress, increase, or growth (in knowledge, virtue, or status)
key_terms.الْإِعْجَابُ: Vanity, self-admiration, or being pleased with oneself to the point of stagnation

ai.seo_question: How does vanity hinder spiritual growth in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identifies al-i'jab (self-admiration) as a subtle spiritual blockage that halts the soul's ascent by fostering complacency. This concept is central to Shia ethical psychology, where pride is viewed not merely as arrogance but as a cessation of the dynamic process of self-purification (tazkiyah). The warning underscores the necessity of continuous humility to maintain receptivity to divine grace and intellectual refinement.
